biography.plain_text: Philippe Foriel-Destezet was a French billionaire who founded the temporary-employment agency Ecco in Lyon. A graduate of HEC Paris, he combined Ecco with Klaus Jacobs’s Adia to create Adecco, building a major international staffing business. He retained a significant shareholding through Akila Finance after stepping down from the group’s co-chairmanship.

confidence.reason: Primary institutional memories and named programme/bequest documentation support the prose.

long_biography.plain_text:
Philippe Foriel-Destezet visited Ecco’s Lyon branches in his Citroën 2CV, sometimes leaving staff unaware that they were meeting the founder. He remained close to former colleagues, returning each year to the Adecco alumni network’s national gathering. His involvement continued beyond his years of executive leadership.

At HEC Paris, Foriel-Destezet contributed to programmes widening access to the business school. He attended the opening of a hall bearing his name with his children, wanting to emphasise a connection across generations. Part of his bequest later funded the HEC Startup Launchpad, which helps final-year students establish their own businesses.
